headline: VMware launches low-end vSphere Express virtualization for up to 128 cores
summary: VMware has released vSphere Express, a new low-end virtualization product supporting up to 128 cores and sold through distributors' marketplaces. Ars Technica quotes a VMware executive saying the company started listening to its lower-end customers, as the Register frames it as an attempt to restore trust with that segment.

claims.statement: VMware released a new low-end virtualization product called vSphere Express, supporting up to 128 cores.

sources.quote: VMware releases vSphere Express for virtualization on up to 128 cores

claims.statement: vSphere Express will be sold through distributors' marketplaces.
A VMware executive said the move came from listening to lower-end customers.

sources.quote: “We started listening to a lot of our lower-end customers," VMware exec says.
